newsitem.title: FRANCE: UN chief Annan optimistic on Zaire talks.
newsitem.headline: UN chief Annan optimistic on Zaire talks.

text.p: U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan said after talks with French Prime Minister Alain Juppe on Thursday that he was optimistic about the prospects for a negotiated settlement of a rebel uprising in eastern Zaire.
"I hope that the discussions in South Africa are going to lead to something...I believe we are on the right path," Annan told reporters after meeting Juppe.

Special UN envoy Mohammed Sahnoun, who was in South Africa for the diplomatic initiative on Zaire launched by President Nelson Mandela, was expected in Paris on Saturday to brief the United Nations chief, Annan said.
Mandela said on Thursday that progress had been made in his separate talks with Zaire's warring parties but kept the details to himself.

Mandela met Mobutu adviser Ngbanda Nzambo Ko Ayumba for an hour in Pretoria on Thursday, a day after talks with rebel leader Laurent Kabila in attempts to get the two sides in roundtable talks and broker a truce.
But a spokesman for Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko told Reuters in Nice, southern France, that Ngbanda was unauthorised to talk on Mobutu's behalf.

The spokesman also denied that Ngbanda was Mobutu's nephew, as he has been widely identified, though the spokesman acknowledged the man was an adviser to Mobutu, Zaire's head of state for the past 31 years.
Mobutu has repeatedly stated his opposition to peace talks before all foreign soldiers have left Zairean soil.

Zaire, which has employed foreign mercenaries to bolster its army, accuses Uganda and Tutsi-led Rwanda and Burundi of fighting with the forces led by rebel leader Laurent Kabila, many of whom are also ethnic Tutsis.
Zaire's three eastern neighbours deny involvement in the conflict, which has sent tens of thousands of local people and Hutu refugees fleeing from Rwanda and Burundi.
Asked about reports of possible new ethnic massacres in the zone of the rebel uprising, Annan said he could not rule this out but had no proof one way or the other.
"You never know. We have seen so many massacres in this region that you cannot exclude the possibility," he said.

The United Nations refugee agency UNHCR said in Geneva on Thursday that it had no confirmation of mass killings in eastern Zaire. But movements of U.N. staff in the region have been restricted by the war.
Juppe reiterated French concerns over the territorial integrity of Zaire and said he believed France could play a role in restoring stability to central Africa's Great Lakes area.
